[Turn 1] USER:
Before do this, I want to understand big picture. I want to understand what we've figured out and what the plan is, because what I don't want us to do is to work ad hoc and not having big plan. Additionally, I would like you to assess how useful the system is, what it tells us. And later on, also we have to think about gardening, because it took us a long time to figure out what's useful in the system, how it works, and we have to make sure that we do remove or at least archive all the old, unnecessary files that are now being kept, so that if anyone approaches the repo, and I would like to share it with some people soon, they would be easy to grab it and not have to reintroduce or have this, do this additional work trying to understand it from ground up as we just did.

[Turn 2] ASSISTANT:
The proposed governing plan treats Lolla as one product with one primary promise: preserve a serious human-LLM conversation, interpret the joint reasoning process, abstract reasoning patterns away from case facts, route those patterns through a curated graph, reattach context for reconsideration, and leave a self-explaining one-run record.

The current system is useful enough to continue because the first fresh run produced an action-level revision. It exposed prestige being treated as evidence, weak commitment signals, a capacity bottleneck, missing evidence gates, and criteria defined after action. The revised answer changed the decision question, sequence, conditions, and stop rules while preserving the user's legitimate urgency. The responsible claim is that Lolla can generate structured challenge pressure and decision-relevant revision with strong process custody. It cannot yet claim stable conversation understanding, unique graph value, better decisions, correctness, or proof of reasoning quality.

The roadmap has two coordinated tracks. Track A proves the core reasoning loop. Track B makes the repository understandable, reproducible, and safe to share. The proposed sequence is Foundation and Gardening first, then Core Semantic Validation, then the reasoning-pattern boundary, graph ablations, gated runtime integration, and finally the strengthened one-run receipt. Cross-run knowledge, organizational memory, Teacher expansion, graph visualization, SDK redesign, and agent continuation remain deferred.

Foundation and Gardening would not immediately delete files or redesign runtime behavior. It would freeze the current state with a tag and hashes, preserve Run 01 and the initial evidence corpus, inventory every file by runtime reachability and retention class, declare Python 3.12 and dependencies, add focused tests and CI, replace the documentation maze with a short canonical reader path, remove personal absolute paths from active surfaces, and define separate code, dataset, and third-party distribution boundaries.

The repository is currently 470 MB with 4,687 tracked files and 1,250 Markdown files. Data is 325 MB, including about 267 MB of compiled affordance snapshots from v1 through v60. Research has 1,579 files; reviews contain 305 Codex-assisted packages and 14 human packages; 263 test files read docs, research, or review paths. README is 1,266 lines and PROGRESS is 4,276 lines. There is no dependency manifest or CI. There are 164 tracked files with absolute /Users paths. The proposed shareable repository would retain live runtime, active substrate, a compact evidence corpus, focused tests, and canonical docs. Historical research, old compiled snapshots, generated review packages, and superseded PR-by-PR documentation would move to an immutable external research archive after hashing and tagging. Raw source briefs and the compiled knowledge substrate would receive a separate rights and distribution review rather than being assumed to fall under the code's MIT license.

The cleanup would be non-destructive and reachability-led. A giant in-repository archive is rejected because it preserves clone and comprehension burden. Dormant Decision Work, Teacher, control-plane, Product Delta, and research machinery would be quarantined and classified before any removal. Old v1-v59 affordance snapshots could leave the product tree only after the v4 fallback consumers are patched or moved with their research tests. Every moved file would retain a manifest entry, hash, destination, reason, and recovery path.

The development phases have explicit gates. Semantic work must show source fidelity and repeatability. Pattern work must show fact invariance and mechanism sensitivity. Graph work must beat direct-critic, labels-only, and disabled or shuffled-edge baselines. Runtime integration must reproduce the offline winner with acceptable cost and latency. Receipt work must let a cold reader distinguish custody, interpretation, challenge execution, revision lineage, and independent review without treating any of them as a quality score.

The recommendation is to approve this blueprint, decide whether the near-term share is private or public, run the freeze and inventory phase, build a share-ready branch without deleting history, resolve dataset and privacy blockers, and only then begin the first semantic-validation implementation slice.
